title: adaptive-evictor-heat-prioritization-and-slab-compactor-runtime-patch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple production escalations across Hosted and Dedicated caused by a compound of memory fragmentation in the slab allocator and a latent KV-cache metadata leak. Customer-facing symptoms: sudden GPU OOMs during burst workloads, long tail latency spikes, and session churn. This ticket tracks the urgent runtime patch (evictor heat prioritization + adaptive slab compactor) plus the canary and rollback plan for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private installs.
incident_timeline: 2025-01-18: First SE report from ACME Analytics (hosted) of sudden task failures followed by GPU OOMs. 2025-01-19: Multiple tenants on Dedicated show cascading restarts during peak. 2025-01-20: Initial triage found slab fragmentation + KV index tombstone growth. 2025-01-21: Hot mitigations (per-tenant circuit-breaker + temporary ticket-based scaling) applied. 2025-01-22: This ticket opened to deliver runtime patch and rollout plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate mixed tenant burst: many small short-lived sessions plus a minority of high-memory long-context sessions. 2) Run with sequence lengths > 2048 and intermittent prefix cache writes. 3) Observe slab allocator not coalescing freed segments; KV index tombstones accumulate and cause allocation pressure leading to GPU allocations failing. 4) Reproduce OOMs within 30-90 minutes of sustained bursts in test harness.
root_cause: The slab allocator's compaction heuristic fails to trigger under a particular pattern: high-rate small allocations interleaved with large infrequent allocations. Meanwhile a KV-cache metadata path that marks keys as tombstoned does not fully release descriptor entries due to a corner-case in the async GC path, causing unseen growth in metadata that prevents slab coalescing. Together these cause allocation failures and elevated tail latency that culminates in GPU OOMs under bursty workloads.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Roll out tenant-level OOM hedging: limit per-tenant concurrent large-session allocations and prefer preemptible burst quota. 2) Activate emergency tombstone sweeper on control plane to reclaim KV descriptors. 3) Increase monitoring and set an automated throttling webhook in Hosted to temporarily circuit-break offending traffic patterns.
long_term_plan: 1) Merge runtime patch: implement evictor heat prioritization (evict KV entries ranked by tenant heat score and recency) and an adaptive slab compactor that runs opportunistically during low-op windows. 2) Fix async GC race that left tombstones unreferenced but not reclaimed. 3) Add unit/integration tests in the stress harness to detect this allocation pattern. 4) Backfill migration for Private instances via a 1-click upgrade bundle.
rollout_strategy: Canary in Hosted: 5% traffic -> 15% -> 50% -> 100% with 4h observation windows. Dedicated: staged node pool rollout starting with non-production pools, then customer opt-in, then forced rollout for customers on the emergency SLA after 7 days. Private: provide hotpatch bundle and a one-step runtime upgrade with preflight checks. Immediate rollback path: toggle runtime flag to disable adaptive compactor + evictor prioritization, and re-enable tombstone sweeper; documented in runbook.
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible GPU OOMs under the stress harness scenario for 72h on canary
KV metadata growth rate returns to baseline (< 5% delta) under burst traces
Tail P99 latency reduced to prior baseline within 10% margin
Automated tests added to regression suite and green in CI
